profile.facility_type_note: Part of QTS's Richmond, Virginia mega-campus, spanning Henrico County and Sandston. This is QTS's flagship facility story: in 2010 QTS converted a former semiconductor manufacturing site into what Wikipedia describes as a 1.3 million square foot mega data center.

reading.body:
DC4 is one of six buildings on the QTS Richmond 1 campus in Sandston, Virginia, a 207-acre site with 2.3 million square feet of current space and 238 MW of total power capacity. The operator publishes no per-building power figure for DC4, so its share of the campus capacity cannot be determined from available sources. At the campus level, 238 MW across 2.3 million square feet implies roughly 0.1 MW per thousand square feet, consistent with a converted semiconductor manufacturing facility rather than a purpose-built AI data center.

Assuming typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, the entire 238 MW Richmond 1 campus could support approximately 5,950 racks of accelerators if fully deployed to that workload. The operator does not publish which tenants occupy DC4 or the campus, which certifications apply to individual buildings, or how the 238 MW is distributed across the six buildings. No per-building specifications appear on operator pages.

Virginia has 326 mapped data center facilities and only 23 with published power capacity totaling 1,375 MW. The Richmond 1 campus ranks 24th in the state by published capacity, below the threshold of published sites. Its position reflects the sparse publication of individual building power figures across the state even at major operators. Whether DC4 matters to AI scaling depends on its actual power draw and tenant mix, neither of which the operator has published.
